comments.body: Even if the tests are green, we need new tests to ensure we are fixing the bug
So it means having tests calling render multiple times on same element
For each widget? Do we really need that?
Well otherwise I can revert your commit and test still green. Every bugfix=test
We didn't test anything when we introduced `dedupe` to solve exactly this issue.

My bad, I was the one introducing `dedupe` and I did not add any tests to it.

I agree we need to have tests to prove that we actually fixed a bug and prevent future regressions. But adding the same tests to all widgets is cumbersome. Does it mean we'll have to add this boilerplate test to all new widgets?

I have no answer to that unfortunatly.
If you're fine with #397 , could we merge it before this one ?

> If you're fine with #397 , could we merge it before this one ?

Yes.

What about testing here? Do we do it or in another PR?
I've rebased on #397 to do the testing since it modified the JSX, but the tests are ready.

@vvo 

> Good, in the end it was not so much boilerplate code to add to test this bug. In the future we might just have a BaseWidget to break a little bit this redundant logic we have (cssClasses)

Well, yes and no, because here we were just missing a `var` keyword, which would have been missing  even if we embedded all the logic in a common function, the issue was present in all widgets.

There's a choice to make, and a little bit of consistency to have here. Do you really want to unit test everything ? If yes, we can't test only once for code that is copy/pasted everywhere. But then we shouldn't only add tests on bug-fixes, but also on every `feat` and `chore` PR.

By the way, I didn't add tests for widgets that I fixed but didn't have a test file.

> But then we shouldn't only add tests on bug-fixes, but also on every feat and chore PR

Oh yes we should have tests for feats that for sure. Then for chore() it depends on the chore, but most probably not because if it's not fixing any bug then there's no test to add (like using let instead of var)

> which would have been missing even if we embedded all the logic in a common function

Yes and we would have had to only add a test to this common function. In the underlying widget you just assume the function is called.

This is unit testing yes so it does not ensures everything, it's hints and ease of developments for us, mostly aimed at if someone removes your code, the test fails and force the dev to re-think/communicate

> Yes and we would have had to only add a test to this common function. In the underlying widget you just assume the function is called.

vs

> Well otherwise I can revert your commit and test still green. Every bugfix=test

Hum ?
